Find what holds up your next salon appointment

Choose one service and model its stages across a working day. Separate the minutes that need a stylist’s hands from the time a client spends processing in a chair. Add wash-basin time where the service uses it. Run the same day twice, changing just one resource, to see whether it makes room for more completed clients.

Manage salon appointments on Shopify →

Worked example

Consider a colour service with 30 minutes of application and 30 minutes of processing. During processing, a second chair can give the stylist somewhere to start another client. Compare one chair with two while leaving the shift, stylist count and wash time unchanged.

Common questions

Why can adding a stylist leave capacity unchanged?

Another stylist can start a client only when the service also has the physical resources it needs. If every chair is occupied during processing, an extra chair may change the schedule more than an extra pair of hands.

Can I use the result to plan a mixed-service salon day?

Each run models clients receiving the same service. Run colour appointments and cuts separately to compare their demands. An actual mixed day also depends on your individual staff shifts, turnaround times and existing bookings.
